subject: Environment
description: Wildlife Protection Act, Forest Conservation Act, EPA, Water/Air Acts, Biological Diversity Act

questions.stem: The WILDLIFE (PROTECTION) ACT of India was enacted in:

options.option_text: 1947, around the time of Indian independence
1972, by the Indira Gandhi government
1986, after the Bhopal gas tragedy disaster
2002, post World Summit on Sustainability

questions.explanation: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 — provides protection to wild animals + plants. Six SCHEDULES: Schedule 1 + 2 give absolute protection (tiger, lion, rhino, etc.); offences attract harshest penalties. Established National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Conservation + Community Reserves, Tiger Reserves. CITES (international convention) implemented through this Act. Amended several times (most recently 2022 — restructured schedules). Distractor 3 = Environment Protection Act (1986, post-Bhopal). Distractor 4 = Biological Diversity Act 2002 (post-Rio).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The ENVIRONMENT (PROTECTION) ACT, 1986 was enacted as a direct response to which event?

options.option_text: The Chipko Movement against deforestation
The Bhopal Gas Tragedy of December 1984
The Stockholm Conference on environment in 1972
The Rio Earth Summit on environment in 1992

questions.explanation: Bhopal Gas Tragedy — 2-3 December 1984. Methyl isocyanate (MIC) leak from Union Carbide pesticide plant. ~3,800 immediate deaths; tens of thousands chronic + delayed. Worst industrial disaster in history. The EPA, 1986 was the legislative response — UMBRELLA Act giving Centre wide powers to set environmental standards, restrict industrial activities, require environmental clearance. Empowers MoEF&CC. Distractor 3 — Stockholm Conference (1972) led to Wildlife Act, Forest Conservation Act, etc. Distractor 4 — Rio led to Biological Diversity Act + various international conventions.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The FOREST CONSERVATION ACT, 1980 specifically restricts which activity?

options.option_text: Hunting of wildlife inside protected forest sanctuaries
De-reservation of forests for non-forest use without Centre
Eco-tourism inside the protected forest reserves of states
Fishing in rivers and streams within forest boundaries

questions.explanation: Forest Conservation Act, 1980 — bars State governments from de-reserving any forest land or using it for non-forest purposes WITHOUT prior approval of the CENTRAL Government. Aim: stop massive forest loss in the post-1947 decades. Process: states must seek 'Forest Clearance' from MoEF&CC for highways, mining, dams, etc. Compensatory afforestation made compulsory; CAMPA fund for that. 2023 amendment (Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act) controversially loosened scope to exclude security/strategic projects in border areas. Distractor 1 = Wildlife Act. Distractor 3, 4 unrelated.

questions.stem: The CENTRAL POLLUTION CONTROL BOARD (CPCB) was established under the:

options.option_text: Air (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act of 1981
Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Environment (Protection) Act of 1986 in India
Forest Conservation Act of 1980 in India

questions.explanation: CPCB — created by the Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. Headquartered in New Delhi. Functions later expanded to AIR pollution by the Air Act, 1981. Sets standards for water + air quality, monitors pollution, issues directives. Functions under the umbrella of MoEF&CC. SPCBs (State Pollution Control Boards) operate at state level. Recent CPCB visibility — Delhi-NCR air-pollution monitoring, GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan), AQI publication.

questions.stem: The NATIONAL GREEN TRIBUNAL (NGT) was established in India by the NGT Act in:

options.option_text: 1986, alongside the EPA umbrella legislation
2010, as a specialised environmental court
1995, after the Rio Earth Summit obligations
2002, alongside the Biological Diversity Act

questions.explanation: NGT Act, 2010 — created the National Green Tribunal as a specialised environmental court. India became the THIRD country (after Australia, New Zealand) with such a court. HQ at New Delhi; benches in Bhopal, Kolkata, Pune, Chennai. Disposes environmental cases within 6 months. Has judicial members (HC judges) + expert members (environmental scientists). Notable orders: ban on 10-year-old diesel + 15-year-old petrol vehicles in Delhi-NCR (2015), Yamuna pollution rulings, halting of various projects without clearance. NGT is expert-driven; criticised by some for over-reach.

questions.stem: The BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY ACT, 2002 of India was enacted to give effect to the:

options.option_text: WTO Agreement on Trade-Related IP Rights
UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), Rio 1992
UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
Vienna Convention on Ozone Layer Protection

questions.explanation: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 — implements India's commitments under the UN CONVENTION ON BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY (CBD, 1992 Rio Earth Summit). Three objectives of CBD: (1) conservation of biological diversity; (2) sustainable use of components; (3) FAIR + EQUITABLE SHARING of benefits arising from use of genetic resources. Three-tier structure in India: NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY AUTHORITY (NBA, Chennai), STATE BIODIVERSITY BOARDS, BIODIVERSITY MANAGEMENT COMMITTEES (BMCs) at panchayat level. Aims to prevent biopiracy (e.g., neem, turmeric patent disputes). Distractor 1 = TRIPS (separate). Distractor 3 = UNFCCC (climate). Distractor 4 = Vienna + Montreal (ozone).

questions.stem: PROJECT TIGER, India's flagship conservation programme, was launched in:

options.option_text: 1947, the year of Indian independence from Britain
1973, during Indira Gandhi's administration
1991, alongside the economic liberalisation reforms
2005, after the National Tiger Conservation Authority

questions.explanation: Project Tiger — launched 1 April 1973 by Indira Gandhi government to save tigers (Panthera tigris tigris, Bengal tiger). Started with 9 tiger reserves; today >55 tiger reserves. 2005-06 — Wildlife Protection Act amended to create the NATIONAL TIGER CONSERVATION AUTHORITY (NTCA) following Sariska tiger crisis (where tigers had vanished due to poaching). Latest tiger census (2022, released 2023): ~3,167 tigers in India — about 75% of the global tiger population. India's flagship conservation success story.
